note: Product-neutral fixtures for registries/operating-model/instance-data-migration.schema.json and scripts/lib/instance-data-migration.mjs. Every `valid` registry must pass evaluateInstanceDataMigration with no problem; every `invalid` registry must produce at least one, when checked with resolvers built from source_snapshot_resolution (makeSourceSnapshotResolver), evidence_resolution (makeEvidenceResolver), rollback_snapshot_resolution (makeRollbackSnapshotResolver), deterministic_plan_resolution (makeDeterministicPlanResolver) and restoration_evidence_resolution (makeRestorationEvidenceResolver) — the five EXTERNAL resolution boundaries this contract checks a 'reproducible' source, a 'verified' sub-verdict and a plan's own rollback (source snapshot, deterministic-reconstruction plan or verified-restoration evidence, whichever rollback.plan requires) against; a bare non-empty ref string (evidence_ref, source_snapshot_ref, deterministic_plan_ref or restoration_evidence_ref alike — including an invented one), or a declared revision/digest with no resolved backing, is never itself accepted as proof. rollback_snapshot_resolution/deterministic_plan_resolution/restoration_evidence_resolution are derived only from the `valid` fixtures' own plans, so they cannot be reused by an `invalid` fixture to accidentally clear the one field it deliberately mutates. plan_fingerprint and idempotency_key values are the real, recomputed output of computePlanFingerprint/computeIdempotencyKey over each fixture's own content — a fixture is not free to pick an arbitrary value; idempotency_key is derived from scope AND the source's repository_ref/revision/digest, not revision alone. No product literals, no absolute machine paths, no dependency on a separate Instance. Digest values are placeholders that satisfy the SHA-256 shape.
